findings.detail: The direct supervisor CLI passes sys.modules[__name__] as the supervisor host module. Under the durable CLI this is the __main__ module. The sealed graph has two roles for the same supervisor source path, host_supervisor19 and supervisor19. During _build_shells, the duplicate-path shell inherits the recorded __main__ name; GraphImportContext.ensure then execs the exact supervisor source into that shell. Its if __name__ == "__main__" guard calls main() recursively. The recursive _load_protocol call enters the frozen dynamic_spec guard with selector v092_replacement19_supervisor_replacement-19 protocol, which has no exact route in that recursive host context, producing the recorded FrozenBridge14Error. This is a CLI host-module identity/entrypoint integration defect; adding a permissive route alias or weakening the route guard would not fix the recursion.
findings.required_correction: Prepare a separately reviewed append-only successor that isolates duplicate graph shells from __main__ using a graph-owned non-main module identity while retaining the exact canonical source path/SHA, host-role identity, graph-local registry and restoration semantics. Preserve the real host module identity needed by the graph, avoid bare process-global aliases or sys.path/importlib bypasses, and keep the exact dynamic-route checks fail-closed. Add a harmless real CLI regression that invokes the supervisor entrypoint through the durable path and reaches a downstream sentinel without re-entering main; include near misses for __main__ shell reuse, foreign module identity and route bypass. Rebind the successor manifest/contract/core/launch controls and require a fresh one-shot invocation review before any retry.
